newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise with Treasury rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise with Treasury rally.

text.p: A benign January U.S. employment report bolstered prices of U.S. mortgage-backed securities on an active Friday, market experts said.

Pass-throughs followed a Treasury rally after the Labor Department's report. Market participants said the jobs report offered fresh relief from any near-term fears of short-term interest rate rise by the Federal Reserve.
"We got some relief from the fears going into the employment number," said one trader. "We underperformed yesterday and we are just getting back today."
Although prices retreated from Friday session highs, pass-throughs were 2/32 to 10/32 higher by late afternoon.
Yield spreads to Treasuries were wider in most coupons earlier in the day, but narrowed as investors gravitated back toward mortgages, traders said.
"As the Treasury market defined its trading range, it took away some fears to the upside and we started to see buyers in the mortgage market," said another trader at a New York Investment bank.
"Customers have been pretty quiet, but we see some CMO (collateralized mortgage obligation) buying," he said.
In Key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was up 9/32 at 100-20/32, yielding 107 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were up 9/32 as well, at 100-16/32 and 100-19/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 15/32 at 100-23/32 to yield 6.40 percent.

The Labor Department reported U.S. payrolls grew by 271,000 in January after 261,000 new jobs were added in December. Meanwhile, the unemployment rate rose to 5.4 percent from 5.3 percent in December, the report said.
